newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foxtel, Optus settle misleading claims with ACCC.
newsitem.headline: Foxtel, Optus settle misleading claims with ACCC.

text.p: Anti-monopolies watchdog the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Thursday it has settled with pay television services Foxtel and Optus Vision over the misleading claims both companies had made.

ACCC said in mid-1996 Optus Vision advertised "20 cents local calls" on television and in newspapers when the service was not widely available. The ACCC felt the promotion was misleading and breached the Trade Practices Act.
Optus Vision is the pay TV arm of Optus Communications.
The ACCC said the matter also related to promotions run by Optus Communications.
In one case Optus produced brochures for its Freestyle mobile phone packages including handsets, which failed to advertise the price of the handsets. One handset cost A$399, the ACCC said.
Apart from its financing of the Fair Call package, Optus has agreed to take far-reaching steps to prevent the recurrence of this conduct, the commision said.

ACCC said Foxtel published a brochure which may have misled consumers about advantages of subscribing to Foxtel's pay television service. The brochure was distributed to over 600,000 addresses in Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide and Brisbane.
In the ACCC's view, the advertisement impiled that only Foxtel subscribers had the special advantage of subscribing to Telstra Flexi-plans and getting cheaper local calls, it said.
In fact, all Telstra customers have access to Flexi-plans, whether they subscribe to pay television or not, it said.

In settlement of ACCC concerns, Foxtel has given an undertaking to broadcast the trade practices compliance infomercial produced by Optus several hundred times on its pay television service, the ACCC said.
ACCC said as a result of the settlements it will launch in July a set of products to help the telecom sector to understand its rights and responsibilities under the Trade Practices Act.
It said the central component is a TV 'infomercial' to be broadcast on five Optus Vision and six Foxtel pay-TV channels.
"The 'infomercial' was orginally part of an out of court settlement negotiated between the ACCC and Optus Vision," ACCC chairman Allan Fels said in a statement.
"A subsequent settlement with Foxtel has permitted its exposure to a wider audience," Fels said.
Foxtel is jointly owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and government owned telephone carrier Telstra Corp Ltd ACCC said the infomercial will also have an internet site http://www.faircall.com.au.
